sanskrit: tato bhāgānubhāgena devagandharvadānavāḥ avatartuṃ mahīṃ sarve rañjayām āsur añjasā
english: Then, by their respective portions and allotments, the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas all descended to the earth and filled it with delight straightway.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samakṣaṃ gandharvīṃ dundubhīṃ nāma nāmataḥ śaśāsa varado devo devakāryārthasiddhaye
english: In their presence the boon-granting god commanded a gandharva woman named Dundubhī, for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose.

sanskrit: pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā gandharvī dundubhī tataḥ mantharā mānuṣe loke kubjā samabhavat tadā
english: Hearing the word of the Grandfather, the gandharva woman Dundubhī then became Mantharā, a hunchback, in the human world.

sanskrit: śakraprabhṛtayaś caiva sarve te surasattamāḥ vānararkṣavarastrīṣu janayām āsur ātmajān te 'nvavartan pitṝn sarve yaśasā ca balena ca
english: And Indra and all those foremost gods begat sons upon the noblest she-monkeys and she-bears; those sons all followed in their fathers' footsteps in both glory and strength.

sanskrit: bhettāro giriśṛṅgāṇāṃ śālatālaśilāyudhāḥ vajrasaṃhananāḥ sarve sarve caughabalās tathā
english: They were breakers of mountain peaks, armed with śāla-trees, palm-trees, and rocks; all of them had frames hard as the thunderbolt, and all possessed power like a rushing torrent.

sanskrit: kāmavīryadharāś caiva sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ nāgāyutasamaprāṇā vāyuvegasamā jave yatrecchakanivāsāś ca ke cid atra vanaukasaḥ
english: All were endowed with valor and prowess at will, all were skilled in battle; their vital breath equaled ten thousand elephants, their speed equaled the wind. Some among these forest-dwellers could live wherever they wished.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidhāya tat sarvaṃ bhagavāṃl lokabhāvanaḥ mantharāṃ bodhayām āsa yad yat kāryaṃ yathā yathā
english: Having arranged all this thus, the blessed lord, sustainer of the worlds, instructed Mantharā concerning every task that had to be done and in what manner.

sanskrit: sā tadvacanam ājñāya tathā cakre manojavā itaś cetaś ca gacchantī vairasaṃdhukṣaṇe ratā
english: She, swift as thought, heeded his word and acted accordingly, going here and there, devoted to kindling enmity.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uktaṃ bhagavatā janma rāmādīnāṃ pṛthak pṛthak prasthānakāraṇaṃ brahmañ śrotum icchāmi kathyatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The birth of Rāma and the others has been told severally by the blessed one; O brahmin, I wish to hear the reason for the departure — please tell it.

sanskrit: kathaṃ dāśarathī vīrau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau prasthāpitau vanaṃ brahma maithilī ca yaśasvinī
english: How were the two heroic brothers, sons of Daśaratha — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — sent to the forest, O brahmin, and the glorious Maithilī as well?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca jātaputro daśarathaḥ prītimān abhavan nṛpaḥ kriyāratir dharmaparaḥ satataṃ vṛddhasevitā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: King Daśaratha, having sons born to him, became joyful — devoted to rites, intent on dharma, ever honoring elders.

sanskrit: krameṇa cāsya te putrā vyavardhanta mahaujasaḥ vedeṣu sarahasyeṣu dhanurvede ca pāragāḥ
english: In time those sons of his grew up, mighty in energy, masters of the Vedas with their secret teachings and of the science of archery.

sanskrit: caritabrahmacaryās te kṛtadārāś ca pārthiva yadā tadā daśarathaḥ prītimān abhavat sukhī
english: When they had completed their celibate studentship and taken wives, O king, then Daśaratha was joyful and content.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭho rāmo 'bhavat teṣāṃ ramayām āsa hi prajāḥ manoharatayā dhīmān pitur hṛdayatoṣaṇaḥ
english: The eldest among them was Rāma; the wise one delighted the people by his captivating nature and gladdened his father's heart.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā matimān matvātmānaṃ vayo 'dhikam mantrayām āsa sacivair dharmajñaiś ca purohitaiḥ
english: Then that wise king, considering himself advanced in years, took counsel with his ministers and with the priests who knew dharma.

sanskrit: abhiṣekāya rāmasya yauvarājyena bhārata prāptakālaṃ ca te sarve menire mantrisattamāḥ
english: Regarding the consecration of Rāma as crown prince, O Bhārata, all those foremost counselors deemed the time had come.

sanskrit: lohitākṣaṃ mahābāhuṃ mattamātaṅgagāminam dīrghabāhuṃ mahoraskaṃ nīlakuñcitamūrdhajam
english: Red-eyed, great-armed, walking like a maddened elephant, long-armed, broad-chested, with dark curling locks —

sanskrit: dīpyamānaṃ śriyā vīraṃ śakrād anavamaṃ bale pāragaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ bṛhaspatisamaṃ matau
english: — blazing with splendor, heroic, in strength not inferior to Indra, a master of all the dharmas, equal to Bṛhaspati in intellect —

sanskrit: sarvānuraktaprakṛtiṃ sarvavidyāviśāradam jitendriyam amitrāṇām api dṛṣṭimanoharam
english: — whose subjects were all devoted to him, who was expert in all branches of knowledge, who had mastered his senses, and whose very appearance charmed even enemies —

sanskrit: niyantāram asādhūnāṃ goptāraṃ dharmacāriṇām dhṛtimantam anādhṛṣyaṃ jetāram aparājitam
english: — a restrainer of the wicked, protector of the righteous, steadfast, unconquerable, a victor who was never defeated —

sanskrit: putraṃ rājā daśarathaḥ kausalyānandavardhanam saṃdṛśya paramāṃ prītim agacchat kurunandana
english: — this son who increased the joy of Kausalyā — King Daśaratha, beholding him, was filled with the greatest delight, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: cintayaṃś ca mahātejā guṇān rāmasya vīryavān abhyabhāṣata bhadraṃ te prīyamāṇaḥ purohitam
english: And that great-souled, mighty one, reflecting on Rāma's virtues, addressed his pleased purohita with the words: "May it go well with you."

sanskrit: adya puṣyo niśi brahman puṇyaṃ yogam upaiṣyati saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhriyantāṃ me rāmaś copanimantryatām
english: "Tonight, O brahmin, the auspicious conjunction of the Puṣya asterism will come; let the requisite materials be gathered, and let Rāma be invited here."

sanskrit: iti tad rājavacanaṃ pratiśrutyātha mantharā kaikeyīm abhigamyedaṃ kāle vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing that word of the king, Mantharā then went to Kaikeyī and at the right moment spoke these words.

sanskrit: adya kaikeyi daurbhāgyaṃ rājñā te khyāpitaṃ mahat āśīviṣas tvāṃ saṃkruddhaś caṇḍo daśati durbhage
english: "Today, O Kaikeyī, the king has made known your great misfortune; a fierce venomous serpent, enraged, bites you, O wretched one."

sanskrit: subhagā khalu kausalyā yasyāḥ putro 'bhiṣekṣyate kuto hi tava saubhāgyaṃ yasyāḥ putro na rājyabhāk
english: "Fortunate indeed is Kausalyā whose son will be consecrated — what fortune is there for you, whose son will not inherit the kingdom?"

sanskrit: sā tad vacanam ājñāya sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā vedīvilagnamadhyeva bibhratī rūpam uttamam
english: She, understanding that speech, adorned with all her ornaments, bearing a most excellent form like an altar-post slender at the waist —

sanskrit: vivikte patim āsādya hasantīva śucismitā praṇayaṃ vyañjayantīva madhuraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: — approached her husband in private, smiling as it were, bright-smiled, expressing affection as it were, and spoke sweet words.

sanskrit: satyapratijña yan me tvaṃ kāmam ekaṃ nisṛṣṭavān upākuruṣva tad rājaṃs tasmān mucyasva saṃkaṭāt
english: "O king of true vows, you once granted me one boon of my desire — fulfill it now, O king, and release yourself from the debt."

sanskrit: rājovāca varaṃ dadāni te hanta tad gṛhāṇa yad icchasi avadhyo vadhyatāṃ ko 'dya vadhyaḥ ko 'dya vimucyatām
english: The king said: "Well then, I grant you the boon — take whatever you wish. Today, who should be executed — let him be executed; who should be released — let him be released."

sanskrit: dhanaṃ dadāni kasyādya hriyatāṃ kasya vā punaḥ brāhmaṇasvād ihānyatra yat kiṃ cid vittam asti me
english: "Today I give wealth to whom it should be given, or let it be taken from whom it should be taken; anything of mine other than brahmin property that exists here."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sā tad vacanam ājñāya parigṛhya narādhipam ātmano balam ājñāya tata enam uvāca ha
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: She, knowing his word and recognizing her own power over the lord of men, embraced him and then spoke thus to him.

sanskrit: ābhiṣecanikaṃ yat te rāmārtham upakalpitam bharatas tad avāpnotu vanaṃ gacchatu rāghavaḥ
english: "Whatever has been prepared for Rāma's consecration — let Bharata receive that; let the Rāghava go to the forest."

sanskrit: sa tad rājā vacaḥ śrutvā vipriyaṃ dāruṇodayam duḥkhārto bharataśreṣṭha na kiṃ cid vyājahāra ha
english: The king, hearing those words so unwelcome and dreadful in consequence, tormented by grief, O foremost of the Bhāratas, said not a single word.

sanskrit: tatas tathoktaṃ pitaraṃ rāmo vijñāya vīryavān vanaṃ pratasthe dharmātmā rājā satyo bhavatv iti
english: Then Rāma, the mighty one, understanding his father thus addressed, set out for the forest — the righteous-souled one saying: "Let the king be true to his word."

sanskrit: tam anvagacchal lakṣmīvān dhanuṣmāṃl lakṣmaṇas tadā sītā ca bhāryā bhadraṃ te vaidehī janakātmajā
english: The glorious bowman Lakṣmaṇa followed him then, as did his wife Sītā — may it go well with you — the Vaidehī, daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: tato vanaṃ gate rāme rājā daśarathas tadā samayujyata dehasya kālaparyāyadharmaṇā
english: Then, when Rāma had gone to the forest, King Daśaratha at that time was united with the law of the body — that which comes in the course of time — and died.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ tu gatam ājñāya rājānaṃ ca tathāgatam ānāyya bharataṃ devī kaikeyī vākyam abravīt
english: Knowing that Rāma had gone and the king had likewise gone, Queen Kaikeyī had Bharata brought and spoke to him.

sanskrit: gato daśarathaḥ svargaṃ vanasthau rāmalakṣmaṇau gṛhāṇa rājyaṃ vipulaṃ kṣemaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam
english: "Daśaratha has gone to heaven; Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are in the forest — take the vast, secure, thorn-free kingdom."

sanskrit: tām uvāca sa dharmātmā nṛśaṃsaṃ bata te kṛtam patiṃ hatvā kulaṃ cedam utsādya dhanalubdhayā
english: The righteous-souled one said to her: "Alas, how cruel a deed you have done — having killed your husband and destroyed this family out of greed for wealth!"

sanskrit: ayaśaḥ pātayitvā me mūrdhni tvaṃ kulapāṃsane sakāmā bhava me mātar ity uktvā praruroda ha
english: "Having cast dishonor upon my head, you destroyer of the family — be content, O my mother" — saying thus, he wept.

sanskrit: sa cāritraṃ viśodhyātha sarvaprakṛtisaṃnidhau anvayād bhrātaraṃ rāmaṃ vinivartanalālasaḥ
english: And having cleansed his conduct in the presence of all the subjects, he followed after his brother Rāma, eager to bring him back.

sanskrit: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ ca suduḥkhitaḥ agre prasthāpya yānaiḥ sa śatrughnasahito yayau
english: Grieving deeply, he had Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī sent ahead in carriages, and he himself went together with Śatrughna.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhavāmadevābhyāṃ vipraiś cānyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ paurajānapadaiḥ sārdhaṃ rāmānayanakāṅkṣayā
english: Together with Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva and thousands of other brahmins and the citizens and country folk, longing to bring Rāma back.

sanskrit: dadarśa citrakūṭasthaṃ sa rāmaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam tāpasānām alaṃkāraṃ dhārayantaṃ dhanurdharam
english: He saw Rāma stationed at Citrakūṭa together with Lakṣmaṇa — an ornament among ascetics, bearing his bow.

sanskrit: visarjitaḥ sa rāmeṇa pitur vacanakāriṇā nandigrāme 'karod rājyaṃ puraskṛtyāsya pāduke
english: Dismissed by Rāma who was acting on his father's word, he administered the kingdom from Nandigrāma, placing Rāma's sandals at the fore.

sanskrit: rāmas tu punar āśaṅkya paurajānapadāgamam praviveśa mahāraṇyaṃ śarabhaṅgāśramaṃ prati
english: But Rāma, fearing another visit of the citizens and country folk, entered the great forest toward the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.

sanskrit: satkṛtya śarabhaṅgaṃ sa daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ nadīṃ godāvarīṃ ramyām āśritya nyavasat tadā
english: Having honored Śarabhaṅga, he took refuge in the Daṇḍaka forest and then dwelt near the lovely river Godāvarī.

sanskrit: vasatas tasya rāmasya tataḥ śūrpaṇakhākṛtam khareṇāsīn mahad vairaṃ janasthānanivāsinā
english: While Rāma was dwelling there, a great enmity arose with Khara, the inhabitant of Janasthāna — owing to what Śūrpaṇakhā had done.

sanskrit: rakṣārthaṃ tāpasānāṃ ca rāghavo dharmavatsalaḥ caturdaśa sahasrāṇi jaghāna bhuvi rakṣasām
english: For the protection of the ascetics, the Rāghava who cherished dharma slew fourteen thousand rākṣasas on the earth.

sanskrit: dūṣaṇaṃ ca kharaṃ caiva nihatya sumahābalau cakre kṣemaṃ punar dhīmān dharmāraṇyaṃ sa rāghavaḥ
english: Having slain Dūṣaṇa and Khara too — those two of immense might — the wise Rāghava once again made the forest of dharma safe.

sanskrit: hateṣu teṣu rakṣaḥsu tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā punaḥ yayau nikṛttanāsoṣṭhī laṅkāṃ bhrātur niveśanam
english: When those rākṣasas were slain, Śūrpaṇakhā then, with her nose and lips cut off, went to Laṅkā, her brother's dwelling.

sanskrit: tato rāvaṇam abhyetya rākṣasī duḥkhamūrchitā papāta pādayor bhrātuḥ saṃśuṣkarudhirānanā
english: Then the rākṣasī, swooning with grief, approached Rāvaṇa and fell at her brother's feet, her face smeared with dried blood.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā vikṛtāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ utpapātāsanāt kruddho dantair dantān upaspṛśan
english: Seeing her thus disfigured, Rāvaṇa was overcome by rage; he sprang from his seat in fury, grinding his teeth together.

sanskrit: svān amātyān visṛjyātha vivikte tām uvāca saḥ kenāsy evaṃ kṛtā bhadre mām acintyāvamanya ca
english: Having dismissed his own ministers, he spoke to her in private: "By whom have you been made thus, dear one, having shown contempt for me without a thought?"

sanskrit: kaḥ śūlaṃ tīkṣṇam āsādya sarvagātrair niṣevate kaḥ śirasy agnim ādāya viśvastaḥ svapate sukham
english: "Who seizes a sharp spear and touches it with every limb? Who places fire upon his head and sleeps in contentment, unsuspecting?"

sanskrit: āśīviṣaṃ ghorataraṃ pādena spṛśatīha kaḥ siṃhaṃ kesariṇaṃ kaś ca daṃṣṭrāsu spṛśya tiṣṭhati
english: "Who touches with his foot the most terrible venomous serpent here? And who touches the maned lion by its fangs and stands there?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bruvatas tasya srotobhyas tejaso 'rciṣaḥ niścerur dahyato rātrau vṛkṣasyeva svarandhrataḥ
english: As he spoke thus, flames of fire issued from his orifices, as sparks issue at night from the hollows of a burning tree.

sanskrit: tasya tat sarvam ācakhyau bhaginī rāmavikramam kharadūṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ rākṣasānāṃ parābhavam
english: His sister told him all of it — Rāma's prowess and the defeat of the rākṣasas together with Khara and Dūṣaṇa.

sanskrit: sa niścitya tataḥ kṛtyaṃ svasāram upasāntvya ca ūrdhvam ācakrame rājā vidhāya nagare vidhim
english: Having resolved on his course of action and consoled his sister, the king set off, having first made the necessary arrangements in the city.

sanskrit: trikūṭaṃ samatikramya kālaparvatam eva ca dadarśa makarāvāsaṃ gambhīrodaṃ mahodadhim
english: Crossing beyond Trikūṭa and also Mount Kāla, he saw the great ocean, deep in its waters, abode of the makara sea-monsters.

sanskrit: tam atītyātha gokarṇam abhyagacchad daśānanaḥ dayitaṃ sthānam avyagraṃ śūlapāṇer mahātmanaḥ
english: Crossing beyond it, the ten-faced one approached Gokarṇa, the beloved and undisturbed abode of the great-souled Śūlapāṇi.

sanskrit: tatrābhyagacchan mārīcaṃ pūrvāmātyaṃ daśānanaḥ purā rāmabhayād eva tāpasyaṃ samupāśritam
english: There the ten-faced one approached Mārīca, his former minister, who had formerly taken to asceticism out of fear of Rāma alone.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca mārīcas tv atha saṃbhrānto dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇam āgatam pūjayām āsa satkāraiḥ phalamūlādibhis tathā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Mārīca then, startled at seeing Rāvaṇa arrive, honored him with hospitality — with fruits, roots, and the like.

sanskrit: viśrāntaṃ cainam āsīnam anvāsīnaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ uvāca praśritaṃ vākyaṃ vākyajño vākyakovidam
english: When he was seated and rested, that rākṣasa sat beside him and spoke respectful words — one skilled in speech addressing one versed in speech.

sanskrit: na te prakṛtimān varṇaḥ kaccit kṣemaṃ pure tava kaccit prakṛtayaḥ sarvā bhajante tvāṃ yathā purā
english: "Your complexion is not its natural self — is all well in your city? Do all your subjects still serve you as before?"

sanskrit: kim ihāgamane cāpi kāryaṃ te rākṣaseśvara kṛtam ity eva tad viddhi yady api syāt suduṣkaram
english: "And what is the purpose of your coming here, O lord of rākṣasas? Know that it is already done, even if it should be most difficult to accomplish."

sanskrit: śaśaṃsa rāvaṇas tasmai tat sarvaṃ rāmaceṣṭitam mārīcas tv abravīc chrutvā samāsenaiva rāvaṇam
english: Rāvaṇa told him all of Rāma's deeds; and Mārīca, having heard, spoke briefly to Rāvaṇa thus.

sanskrit: alaṃ te rāmam āsādya vīryajño hy asmi tasya vai bāṇavegaṃ hi kas tasya śaktaḥ soḍhuṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: "Enough of confronting Rāma — I know his valor well. Who indeed can bear the speed of that great-souled one's arrows?"

sanskrit: pravrajyāyāṃ hi me hetuḥ sa eva puruṣarṣabhaḥ vināśamukham etat te kenākhyātaṃ durātmanā
english: "That bull among men is indeed the very cause of my renunciation. This is the mouth of destruction for you — by what wicked soul has it been told to you?"

sanskrit: tam uvācātha sakrodho rāvaṇaḥ paribhartsayan akurvato 'smadvacanaṃ syān mṛtyur api te dhruvam
english: Then Rāvaṇa, full of anger, spoke to him with harsh reproof: "Death will certainly be yours if you do not carry out my command."

sanskrit: mārīcaś cintayām āsa viśiṣṭān maraṇaṃ varam avaśyaṃ maraṇe prāpte kariṣyāmy asya yan matam
english: Mārīca reflected: "When death inevitably comes, a better death is preferable — I shall do what is his intention."

sanskrit: tatas taṃ pratyuvācātha mārīco rākṣaseśvaram kiṃ te sāhyaṃ mayā kāryaṃ kariṣyāmy avaśo 'pi tat
english: Then Mārīca replied to that lord of rākṣasas: "What assistance of mine is needed by you? I will do it, even helplessly."

sanskrit: tam abravīd daśagrīvo gaccha sītāṃ pralobhaya ratnaśṛṅgo mṛgo bhūtvā ratnacitratanūruhaḥ
english: The ten-necked one said to him: "Go and entice Sītā — become a deer with jeweled horns, with a body variegated with gems."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ sītā samālakṣya tvāṃ rāmaṃ codayiṣyati apakrānte ca kākutsthe sītā vaśyā bhaviṣyati
english: "Sītā will certainly, upon seeing you, urge Rāma on; and when the Kākutstha has gone forth, Sītā will be in my power."

sanskrit: tām ādāyāpaneṣyāmi tataḥ sa na bhaviṣyati bhāryāviyogād durbuddhir etat sāhyaṃ kuruṣva me
english: "I will carry her away, and then that evil-minded one will cease to be, due to separation from his wife. Render me this assistance."

sanskrit: ity evam ukto mārīcaḥ kṛtvodakam athātmanaḥ rāvaṇaṃ purato yāntam anvagacchat suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Mārīca performed his water-rite, and then, deeply grieved, followed after Rāvaṇa who went ahead.

sanskrit: tatas tasyāśramaṃ gatvā rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ cakratus tat tathā sarvam ubhau yat pūrvamantritam
english: Then, having gone to the hermitage of Rāma of untiring deeds, the two of them did all that which had been previously planned.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tu yatir bhūtvā muṇḍaḥ kuṇḍī tridaṇḍadhṛk mṛgaś ca bhūtvā mārīcas taṃ deśam upajagmatuḥ
english: Rāvaṇa became a wandering mendicant — shaven-headed, carrying a water pot and triple staff; and Mārīca, having become a deer, the two approached that place.

sanskrit: darśayām āsa vaidehīṃ mārīco mṛgarūpadhṛk codayām āsa tasyārthe sā rāmaṃ vidhicoditā
english: Mārīca, wearing the deer's form, displayed himself to the Vaidehī; she, impelled by fate, urged Rāma for the sake of it.
